channel.description: Latest articles from Cato Institute – Bias and Credibility (cato.org)

item.title: Analyzing the Trump Administration’s National Policy Framework for AI
item.description: In general, however, this approach signals that the administration remains committed to the idea that the light-touch approach to regulation that allowed America to lead in the internet age remains the best solution to continued leadership in the AI era.

item.title: Brian Doherty, In Memoriam
item.description: Twenty-four hours in a day seemed to be too few for him, and he always seemed to try to do as much in the time that he had—his voracious reading habits were legendary. I just wish that he had had more time with the rest of us here.

item.title: Muslim Immigrants Assimilate Even More Than Polls of Muslims Indicate
item.description: It is important to understand that Muslims do assimilate. In prior posts on this topic, I have shown how this pattern repeats on a variety of other issue areas—including support for violence against civilians, which Muslims are less supportive of than the general population.

item.title: Senate Approach to Section 230 Would Eviscerate the Internet and Online Expression
item.description: Section 230 was the cornerstone that allowed the internet to become a massive marketplace of ideas, products, and services. It remains essential today, as without it, companies would stagnate and die under ruinous liability.

item.title: Primary Care Shortages Are Driving Patients to AI—Will Regulators Stand in the Way?
item.description: Loosening the FDA’s approach to software-based medical tools would not replace clinicians, but it could empower patients and extend the reach of care to millions who currently fall through the cracks. At a time when the system is strained, policymakers should be looking for ways to enable innovation, so fewer patients are left to navigate it alone.

item.title: Obamacare at 16: There's No Reason Not to Provide Consumers Relief
item.description: The arguments against Obamacare relief do not comport with the available evidence.

item.title: The Remedy-Free Zone: Reclaiming State Power to Curb Federal Misconduct
item.description: State-law remedies merely provide a way to enforce existing federal rights; an unconstitutional act is, by definition, outside the scope of lawful authority.

item.title: No, Credit Card Interest Rate Caps Won't Help Consumers
item.description: We do not live in a simple world where the intent behind a law magically prevents unintended consequences. Luckily, we do live in a world where we know the downside of interest rate caps.

item.title: Postal Service Out of Cash
item.description: The best reform would be for Congress to privatize the USPS and give company managers the flexibility to make reforms based on cost factors and consumer demands.

item.title: Rare Earths, Vulcan, and Government Equity Stakes
item.description: While the US has strategic supply chain concerns, federal ownership of private companies is both unnecessary and undesirable.
